evidence.requirements: Nearly every requirement is met. The start page has the heading, name links, family, L3, Search, the Family select and the 'n cartridges' count (app.js:25-73, list.jpg). The detail view has every fact, the capacity source link, Symbol/Value/Unit tables, Print and 'All cartridges', and hash routes that survive a reload (app.js:98-171). Tolerances sit next to their values ('39.62 -0.2', '5.59 -0.2' in detail-300_win_mag.jpg) and the symbol mapping is right (format.js:5-9). All the required dimensions are drawn, plus the title block with scale, hatched section, dash-dot centre line and accessible name. The print layout fits one A4 page (print-308_win.jpg). Missing values are listed in the figcaption (app.js:135). Partly met: on straight cases the wall is blended linearly from tb to tn along the whole body (geometry.js:212); the brief says tb along the body. The groove rule only applies to rimless, rebated and belted rims (geometry.js:137); the brief says 'where E and E1 are published'. This has no effect on the 25 records. The configured spec tool was not used: openspec/specs holds only .gitkeep.
evidence.correctness: The geometry follows the rules closely. Rim type uses the 1.05 and 0.98 thresholds (geometry.js:102). The chamfer uses min(f·tanβ, R1/4) (geometry.js:122). The groove and belt ramp at δ: zEnd = R+eMin+(R3/2−E1/2)/tanδ (geometry.js:151). The rimfire half-round radius is min(R/2,(R1−P1)/2), with its outermost point at R1/2. The shoulder fillets with r1 min and r2 are real tangent arcs (geometry.js:27-42). The tangent ogive ρ and its centre, the quarter-ellipse and cone noses, the s/k/m tables by shape and category, and the heeled 22 LR (exposed bullet at H2, heel at H2−2tb) are all right. The tn/tb walls, w = max(...), and the pocket diameter and depth tables are right too. Compared with the reference drawings, 308_win, 300_win_mag, 9_mm_luger and 22_long_rifle match in outline and proportions. The 44 Rem. Mag. semi-wadcutter shows a short cylinder and a cone to a large meplat. Label values match the data ('L3 51.18', 'α 10°58'0"'). Small deviations: the straight-case wall taper is invented (geometry.js:212); it makes the 9 mm wall at the bullet base about 0.38 mm instead of 0.6. Diameter dimension lines run across both halves, so the R1/E1/P1 arrowheads crowd together at the head (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg). The print test asserts one page for all 25 records (tests/e2e/drawing.test.js:117-137).
evidence.security: The only innerHTML is the SVG string (app.js:131). Every data string in it goes through esc() (drawing.js:18), and numbers go through n(). The rest of the DOM uses textContent and createElement (app.js:8-16). There is no eval or Function, no fetch, no CDN and no web font. An e2e test asserts there are no external requests (app.test.js:84-85).
evidence.code_quality: Four small IIFE modules with clear roles: format (pure), geometry (pure, no DOM), drawing (string SVG plus label boxes) and app (views and router). The names follow the brief's symbols. Missing values are collected as data instead of being thrown. Label placement is a bounded depth-first search (drawing.js:59-90), which is somewhat intricate but commented. Minor blemishes: odd indentation at drawing.js:174, has() and rMaxAt() defined after use at the bottom of drawing.js, and some long one-line expressions (geometry.js:131).
evidence.tests: There are node:test unit tests and Playwright e2e tests. Geometry tests check exact outline points for chamfer, groove, belt, rimmed step and straight case, plus walls, w, pocket tables, bullet s/k/m for each shape, the heeled bullet, ogive tangency and missing-value reporting (geometry.test.js). E2E tests check, for all 25 records, that labels do not overlap each other or the sampled outline, that dimensions have arrows and extension lines, 1 unit = 1 mm, the title block, one PDF page per record, white print background and hidden navigation. They also cover file:// and http, search by alternative name, family counts, reload of the address, and phone width without overflow. Gaps: no checks of fillet radii, chamfer on rimmed cases, the α arc geometry, or the straight-case wall rule.
evidence.ux_design: The screens are dense and calm. The facts sit in a two-column dl, values are in monospace with tabular numbers, and the compact section tables use captions (detail-308_win.jpg). The drawing is legible and its labels are clear of the outline. The print page is one A4 sheet with the h1, drawing, four-column tables and source footer (print-308_win.jpg). Weaknesses: the title block is oversized on screen and takes about a third of the drawing panel (detail-22_long_rifle.jpg). The cartridge uses only 60–70% of the panel width. The arrowheads cluster at the head on short cases. The Water capacity row in the print facts grid is oddly aligned. Dark mode exists in CSS (style.css:17-30) but has no screenshot to judge it by.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img, aria-label '<name> drawing', a <title>, and a <desc> that lists every labelled dimension (drawing.js:185-189). Tables have captions and th with scope col/row (app.js:85-89). Search and Family have real <label for> elements. The count is a polite live region. Focus moves to the h1 on navigation (app.js:169-170). focus-visible outlines are styled, and the muted grey #5a626b on #fbfbf8 has good contrast. There is no skip link, and the small uppercase table headers (.72rem) are a minor legibility cost.
evidence.simplicity: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no runtime dependencies and no build step. The data is a classic script so the app works from file:// (data.js:1-2). Playwright is the only dev dependency. The app code is about 1,000 lines in total, which fits the problem.
evidence.maintainability: There is no README, no docs, no ADRs and no CI configuration. openspec/specs contains only .gitkeep. package.json has test scripts, but playwright is a caret range (^1.50.0); there is a lockfile but no engines field or .nvmrc for Node 22. helper.js:1-2 mentions an undocumented manual step ('npx playwright install chromium', LD_LIBRARY_PATH). There is no release or versioning approach beyond 1.0.0. The code itself is readable and the tests are a solid regression net.
evidence.visual_design: Restrained palette with a blue accent for dimensions, ink-black outlines and a beige bullet section. Typography is consistent: system sans for the page and monospace for the drawing and values. Small uppercase table headers, aligned numeric columns and consistent spacing across all six detail screenshots. The heavy, very large title-block type looks out of scale with the drawing labels.
evidence.layout: The hierarchy is clear: name, facts, drawing, actions, then tables in a responsive three-column grid (detail-*.jpg). There is no overlap or clipping in any screenshot. The Print and All cartridges actions sit below a tall drawing panel instead of near the heading. The drawing panel leaves whitespace to the sides of short cartridges (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, detail-22_long_rifle.jpg).
evidence.usability: Search as you type works with spacing-insensitive matching ('22LR', '7,62 x 51'). Alternative names show next to the link in the list. The family filter and count give instant feedback, and there is an empty-state message. Detail addresses can be bookmarked, and an unknown key gives 'Cartridge not found' with a way back. Print is one click to a clean one-page sheet. The list cannot be sorted, and the back link is below the drawing.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would find this credible. Values appear as published, tolerances sit inline, the scale is honest, missing values are named instead of invented, and the print output is clean on one page. The rule-based proportions match the OpenBallistics references. The oversized title block and crowded head arrowheads are cosmetic, not trust-breaking.

unmet_requirements: Straight-case section wall is blended from tb to tn along the whole body (geometry.js:212) instead of tb along the body as the rule states
Extractor groove rule is limited to rimless, rebated and belted rim types (geometry.js:137) instead of applying wherever E and E1 are published (no effect on the given data)
Process: the configured spec tool was not used (openspec/specs holds only .gitkeep); no README or docs
strengths: Faithful implementation of the geometry rules: tangent shoulder fillets, a correct tangent ogive, belt ramp at δ, heeled rimfire bullet, wall and head rules. Outlines match the reference drawings in proportion.
Strong automated verification: no label collisions across all 25 drawings, one A4 PDF page per cartridge, 1 unit = 1 mm, file:// and http, and no external requests.
Secure, dependency-free, compact code. Data is rendered as published, with inline tolerances, the specified angle formats and named missing values.
issues: No README, docs, ADRs, specs or CI. Node and Playwright are not pinned exactly, and Chromium install / LD_LIBRARY_PATH are undocumented manual steps.
The straight-case section uses an invented tb→tn wall taper along the whole body (geometry.js:212), which deviates from the rule and makes the 9 mm wall at the bullet base thinner than tb.
On-screen drawing presentation: the title block is oversized relative to the drawing. Full-diameter dimension lines cross the section and crowd the R1/E1/P1 arrowheads at the head of short cases.
review.verdict: A careful, accurate and well-tested implementation: the drawings follow the brief's rules and match the reference proportions, the tables show data exactly as published, and the print view reliably fits one A4 page. Before publishing it needs a README and CI so others can maintain it, plus small fixes to the straight-case wall rule and the drawing's visual balance.
